messages:
sam: Heads-up — I merged the TF change that tweaks the Karpenter provisioner constraints and updates the HPA target for the frontend service. After the deploy, we noticed no scale-ups when load jumped. Can someone quick-check metrics wiring?

maria: Do you mean the HPA isn't evicting/creating pods, or Karpenter not provisioning nodes? :thinking:

sam: HPA stays at desired=1 even under 300% CPU. Karpenter also didn't spin up new nodes (no pending pods).

kevin: Could be custom metrics adapter. The frontend HPA uses a prometheus metric (req_per_second). If prometheus-adapter is misconfigured the HPA falls back to CPU only and our CPU target is low.

sam: Right — HPA spec uses: 
```yaml
metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: frontend_req_rate
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "200"
```

liz: Quick checks: 
- `kubectl get hpa frontend -o yaml`
- `kubectl get --raw "/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1"` to confirm adapter exposes metric
- logs for prometheus-adapter: `kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/prometheus-adapter`

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] rollout: service/frontend v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2 (sam) at 1923512346 :rocket:

maria: Also check RBAC for prometheus-adapter — the adapter needs to query Prometheus. We recently rotated the monitoring secrets and the adapter SA might lack the new secret name.

kevin: If the adapter fails, you'll see no entries under `/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io` for the metric name. Another quick test: `kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1 | jq .`

sam: Ran that: `/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io` returns 404. prometheus-adapter logs show: 
```
E0321 14:12:10.123 adapter.go:72] could not scrape metrics: error fetching from prometheus: unauthorized (401)
```

maria: Ah — unauthorized. Which secret is the adapter using for Prometheus? Our PR changed the monitoring secret path in TF from `monitoring/prom-read` -> `monitoring/prom-frontend-read` to scope per-namespace. Adapter might still reference old path.

liz: The Helm values we deploy for prometheus-adapter pull `prometheus.readSecretName` from the k8s secret `monitoring/prom-frontend-read`. If TF renamed the secret, helm release needs to be updated.

kevin: Short-term fix: set HPA to CPU target so scaling uses node CPU while we fix adapter. Eg: 
```yaml
spec:
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 60
```
But note that will cause scale-ups based on pod CPU which may be noisy.

sam: I'll revert the TF change for the monitoring secret and trigger a helm redeploy of prometheus-adapter, unless someone objects. Want to avoid rollback of Karpenter changes if not necessary.

maria: +1 to revert secret rename and re-run CD for adapter. After adapter healthy, confirm `/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io` lists `frontend_req_rate`.

kevin: Also add a short-lived HPA annotation to prevent scale-to-zero while we validate: `autoscaling.alpha.kubernetes.io/behavior: '{"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 300}}'` or just bump minReplicas to 2 for frontend.

sam: Will do: I'll open a tiny revert PR for TF secret name and patch the helm release for adapter. I'll also temporarily set frontend.minReplicas=2.

liz: After adapter is healthy, please run this to sanity-check metrics mapping: 
```bash
kubectl get --raw "/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/default/frontend_req_rate" | jq .
```
We should see a JSON with values.

sam: Filed PRs: 1923512400 (tf-revert-monitoring-secret) and 1923512420 (helm-prom-adapter-redeploy). Patching frontend minReplicas in a hotfix at 1923512440.

maria: Thanks. Once adapter redeploys, ping here with logs line `adapter.go:.*scrape.*ok` or `/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io` output. :thumbsup:

kevin: If anyone sees Karpenter Pod Trafficslim errors after nodes come up, check provisioner TTL and node template taints. Our TF tweak lowered `ttlSecondsAfterEmpty` to 30s in the provisioner which might churn nodes under bursty load — consider 300s.

sam: noted, will avoid changing TTL in the revert.

liz: If we need, I can run an on-call runbook for HPA troubleshooting (short checklist).

sam: Update: prometheus-adapter redeploy succeeded, logs show `scrape: ok` at 1923512455. `/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io` now lists `frontend_req_rate`. HPA responded and desired scaled to 4; Karpenter created 2 nodes.

maria: :tada: Great. Follow-ups: 1) add a CI check that TF secret renames must update helm values (or fail deploy), 2) add an alert when `/apis/external.metrics.k8s.io` returns 5xx/401.

kevin: Agree on both. I'll open a GH issue for the CI check.

sam: Thanks all. I'll close the revert PRs once the rollout stabilizes (monitoring for 15m).
